name: Third World
scope: The Third World as a political idea, as the defining sources present it: the emancipatory, anticolonial and internationalist project of the formerly colonised and non-aligned states of Asia, Africa and Latin America from the Bandung Conference (1955) through the Tricontinental (1966) and the 1974 call for a New International Economic Order, with its demands for self-determination, non-interference, non-alignment in the Cold War, South-South cooperation and a fairer world economy. It does not cover the term as a mere economic label for poor countries or as a geographic list (Yapp's second and third senses), Mao's Three Worlds Theory, nor the narrower doctrines with their own entries (third-worldism, Third World socialism, Maoist third-worldism).

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Non-interference in the internal affairs of other States is a core principle (Bandung; declaration 4a), which arming insurgents breaches.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Principle 4f of the declaration gives peoples under colonial domination a right to restitution and full compensation for the exploitation and depletion of their resources.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Third World project is anticolonial throughout: it sought to demolish empires, and the declaration condemns colonial domination and the exploitation of colonial resources.

defeat-communism.rationale: Bandung reiterated peaceful coexistence and the nonaligned movement refused to take sides in the Cold War, so putting defeat of communism ahead of coexistence contradicts it.

dominated-front.rationale: The sources present the Third World as a call to solidarity among formerly colonised peoples, with Bandung aiming at cooperation among them and less reliance on Europe and North America.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: Non-interference in internal affairs is a core Bandung principle and principle 4a of the 1974 declaration.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Fanon's conclusion urges the Third World not to create states, institutions and societies that draw their inspiration from Europe.

military-force-for-human-rights.rationale: Non-interference in other States' internal affairs is a core principle (Bandung; declaration 4a), which military action abroad would breach.

nation-first.rationale: The declaration bases the new order on common interest, interdependence and the broadest cooperation among all States; putting one country's interests ahead of cooperation runs against that.

national-mission.rationale: Non-interference and each country's right to choose its own economic and social system (declaration 4a, 4d) exclude a mission to spread one's form of government abroad.

national-resource-control.rationale: The 1974 New International Economic Order declaration (principle 4e) states every State's full permanent sovereignty over its natural resources, with effective control and the right to nationalise them.

national-self-determination.rationale: Self-determination of all peoples is a core principle in both the Bandung programme and the 1974 declaration (4a); the declaration says it for peoples, not for every self-defined nation's own state.

racial-franchise.rationale: Bandung called for an end to racial discrimination wherever it occurred; a vote limited to one ethnic group contradicts that.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Bandung called for an end to racial discrimination wherever it occurred, and the declaration backs peoples under racial domination and apartheid.

recognize-territorial-claims-from-conque.rationale: The declaration states the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territories by force (4a).

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The 1974 declaration proclaims a New International Economic Order to correct inequalities, with preferential non-reciprocal treatment for developing countries and fairer commodity prices (4j, 4n).

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The declaration calls for active assistance to developing countries by the whole international community, free of political or military conditions (4k), and for resource transfers (4o).

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The Office of the Historian says Bandung led to the nonaligned movement, whose leaders banded together to avoid being forced to take sides in the Cold War.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The declaration lists the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territories by force among its founding principles (4a).

summary: The Third World, as an idea, was the political project of the formerly colonised and non-aligned states of Asia, Africa and Latin America: an internationalist demand to end empire, to keep out of the Cold War blocs, to uphold sovereignty and non-interference, and to remake the world economy in favour of developing countries (Bandung 1955, the 1974 New International Economic Order). It was a coalition of states and intellectuals rather than a full social programme, so its sources are silent on most domestic questions.
